title: Adaptive load bench and percentile drift alerts by endpoint / model / region
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: Provide per-endpoint/model/region percentile tracking (p50/p95/p99) with heatmaps and automated regression detection tied to synthetic and production-derived load profiles. Deliverables include: 1) an adaptive load harness that can generate tokens/sec mixes matching production distributions (by prompt length, model family, request signature), 2) percentile rollup pipeline that attributes p95/p99 regressions to route+model+region slices and cohorts, 3) Grafana dashboard set with heatmaps + timelines and an alerting workflow for regressions that integrates with PagerDuty and ticket creation. Why: current dashboards surface rollups but often hide cohort regressions (e.g., long-prompt tails for a specific model in eu-west). This work reduces MTTI for tail latency regressions and provides reproducible benchmark artifacts for postmortems and performance PRs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Synthetic harness can replay three production-derived workload profiles (chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-bulk) against any endpoint+model+region and produce tokens/sec and latency distributions. 2) Telemetry pipeline computes p50/p95/p99 per minute and writes slice keys (route, model, region, prompt_length_bucket) to the quantile store. 3) Dashboards: a) heatmap of p95/p99 across models (x) and regions (y) with time slider; b) cohort explorer for prompt_length_bucket and client_id; c) tokens/sec vs p95 correlation panel. 4) Regression detector flags anomalous p95/p99 deviations above rolling baseline (configurable, default: 20% relative increase and 30ms absolute) and creates a ticket with top contributing slices. 5) End-to-end test and runbook completed; smoke run demonstrates detection on seeded regression and dashboard panels render without >5s timeouts.
design_notes: - Use existing quantile aggregation job as baseline but extend to emit per-slice histograms for p95/p99 bootstrap estimation. - Adaptive load harness will sample from a production request signature histogram (anon) to preserve token length and model mix. - To avoid metric explosion, only materialize slices above an activity threshold (default 1000 requests/day) and provide on-demand narrow queries for low-volume slices. - Use reservoir sampling to keep representative synthetic traces for replay. - Consider two regression detectors: 1) statistical (EWMA + bootstrap confidence) for sensitivity to small shifts, 2) windowed ratio detector for large abrupt changes. - Prioritize low cardinality slice keys in runtime pipeline for cost control; use coarse prompt_length_bucket (<=32,33-128,129-512,>512).
work_items: Implement adaptive synthetic load runner (go) with profile ingestion
Extend quantile rollup job to include slice labels and histogram snapshots
Add alerting rule and PagerDuty integration for percentile regressions
Create Grafana dashboards and reusable panels
Add e2e smoke test that seeds a 30% p95 regression and verifies detection

risks: Metric cardinality blowup if too many slices materialized
False positives from noisy low-volume slices
Synthetic harness may not fully replicate production cache/topology effects
rollback_plan: If alert noise or storage costs exceed thresholds: 1) disable regression alerts (runtime flag), 2) reduce retention for histogram snapshots to 7d, 3) only emit p95/p99 at 5-minute granularity instead of 1-minute, 4) revert quantile rollup changes and rerun backfill for a minimal subset of slices.
test_plan: Unit tests for quantile aggregation code
Integration test: run synthetic harness against staging endpoint and validate p95/p99 within +/-15% of production baseline
E2E: seed synthetic 30% p95 regression and validate automatic ticket + dashboard link
next_steps: Finish dashboard panels and alert templates -> run controlled smoke regression -> onboard two pilot teams (console and dedicated) for two weeks -> iterate thresholds and false-positive filters.
